statement.p: Find the exact solution to the equation below. (Do not give a decimal approximation.)

static.solution:
SOLUTION
First we isolate the natural log:
\ \ \ \ \ \ \ 5 \ln{(2 x + 2)} = 16
\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ln{(2 x + 2)} = \frac{16}{5}
Now we can rewrite in exponential form and solve for x:
\ \ \ \ \ \ \ 2 x + 2 = e^{16/5}
\ \ \ \ \ \ \ 2 x = e^{16/5} - 2
\ \ \ \ \ \ \ x = \frac{ e^{16/5} - 2 }{2}.
Now we check our solution:
\ \ \ \ \ \ \ 5 \ln{ \bigg( 2 \left( \frac{ e^{16/5} - 2 }{2} \right) + 2 \bigg) } = 5 \ln{ \left( (e^{16/5} - 2) + 2 \right)}
\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ = 5 \ln{(e^{16/5})} = 5 \cdot \left( \frac{16}{5} \right) = 16
which is the result we want.
